verdict.rationale: Metorial documents publishable vs. secret API keys and per-environment keys, which give coarse credential scoping. Sessions can also be restricted with allow-list tool filters and expose a connection URL for an MCP client, giving an agent a narrowed tool surface. However, no documentation shows per-key permission scopes, expiry, or fine-grained least-privilege policies on the API credentials themselves. Missing for 10: fine-grained per-key scopes/permissions, key expiry/rotation controls, explicit agent-specific credential issuance, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can generate both publishable and secret API keys in your Metorial dashboard by navigating to Developer → API Keys and clicking Create API Key.
Each environment has its own provider deployments, API keys, authentication configs, and logs, so changes in a sandbox do not affect production.
Tool filters let you control which tools from a provider are available during a session.
Instead of sharing broad credentials or over-scoped service accounts, each user connects their own apps and keeps the permissions they should have.
